component.name: Notterizmus
component.summary: Outline editor for book chapter notes

description.p: Notterizmus is an outline editor for taking notes on book chapters. It numbers items automatically (Ⅰ, Ⅰ.1, Ⅰ.1.a) and draws tree lines between them, and it copies the result as formatted text that pastes cleanly into TopCoding.

ul.li: Automatic numbering with Unicode Roman numerals and tree connectors
Bullets for notes, pros and cons; bold, italic, tables and Excalidraw drawings
Paste that recognises outline structure and renumbers it
Undo and redo for text and structure, selection scopes and multiple cursors
Spell checking in English and Bulgarian, chosen per chapter
One autosaved file per book chapter

description.p: Mouse selection, pasted tables and sturdier file handling.

ul.li: Dragging the mouse from one item to another selects whole items, scrolling at the window's edge.
A table copied on its own, or with plain text, is pasted after the current item.
A damaged chapter or settings file is reported instead of keeping the app from starting.
Renumbering, reordering and renaming handle chapters that can't be read or written without losing track of files.
Deleting a top-level item turns its bullets into numbered items.

description.p: Fixes for text, find and earlier versions.

ul.li: Thin strokes stay visible: the top bar of "=" no longer fades so that it looks like "-".
Escape closes the find bar from anywhere in it and from the text.
Ctrl+F on a selected word starts at that word, Search Commands keeps the selection for Bold and Italic, and Enter right after typing acts on what was typed.
Earlier Versions keeps a long history: all of the last day, then one copy per hour, per day and per week as they get older, grouped by day.
Indenting or outdenting an item whose text wraps no longer makes the rows below jump.

description.p: Finding things, earlier versions, and a bigger or smaller text.

ul.li: Find (Ctrl+F) and replace (Ctrl+H or Ctrl+R) across the chapter, table cells included, with Match Case and Whole Words. Replace All is one undo step.
Earlier Versions in the menu: a copy of each chapter is kept when you open it and every 10 minutes while you edit. Preview one and restore it; Ctrl+Z takes it back.
Search Commands (Ctrl+Shift+P) finds any command by name, runs it and shows its key.
Text size: Ctrl+=, Ctrl+- and Ctrl+0, Ctrl with the scroll wheel, or the row at the top of the menu. Only the chapter's text changes.

description.p: Moving around your books, and learning the controls.

ul.li: A chapter list on the left shows every book with its chapters (F9). Ctrl+PgUp and Ctrl+PgDn open the previous or next chapter, and the list's edge can be dragged to resize it.

Chapter Properties (F2) renames a chapter, changes its number or moves it to another book; F2 on a book renames the book. Drag chapters or press Alt+Up and Alt+Down in the list to reorder them; Delete moves one to the Trash, with Undo.
Getting Started (F1) opens a practice chapter that shows each control. About is now only in the menu.
Chapters saved by a newer version open safely: parts this version doesn't know are kept unchanged and shown read-only.
Fixed warnings printed for chapters with tables.

description.p: Typing aids and a scrolling fix.

ul.li: Ctrl+Space shows spelling fixes and completes the word at the cursor from the chapter, the book's other chapters and the dictionary. Changing an item's type moved to Ctrl+Shift+Space.
Number hotkeys 1–9 and 0 in the Alt+Insert, item and Ctrl+Space popups.
The view follows the cursor, so pressing Enter at the bottom of a full window no longer hides it.
